RFC3786-3.2.1-1.no_code_path: The ban binds the originator of an Extended LSP (Mode 1 virtual-system operation). Owner decision 2026-09-21 'Keep standard fragment sets': Ze has no Mode 1 configuration, no virtual-system adjacency and no extended-LSP producer (internal/plugins/isis/config.go, lsdb/origination.go), so no code path can specify a neighbor in an Extended LSP. Mirrors RFC3786-x-2.
RFC3786-3.2.1-1.note: Judged 2026-09-30. {not-applicable} accepted; the child spec constraint records x-2's split as a row-text decision.

RFC3786-5-1.note: Row narrowed to the Original-set sentences. Missing fragment 0: TestRFC1195StandardFragmentsRequireFragmentZero requires the fragment-1 route while fragment 0 lives (2, 15) and no route after fragment 0 is deleted. RemainingLifetime zero: TestRFC3786ExpiredFragmentZeroExcludesSet stores a zero-lifetime fragment 0, asserts it is still held by the LSDB, and requires no route although fragment 1 still carries the link back and the prefix. Whole-stack: RawSnapshot drops zero-lifetime entries and Records admits no fragment of a source without a live fragment 0. The extended-set clause is RFC3786-5-2.

RFC3786-5-2.no_code_path: internal/plugins/isis/lsdb/origination.go caps a source at maxFragments = 256 standard fragments and no IS Alias ID TLV (type 24) is decoded or originated in internal/plugins/isis/packet, so no extended LSP set exists; internal/plugins/isis/spf_wiring.go Records groups fragments by source ID only. The condition 'fragment 0 of an extended LSP set' never holds.
RFC3786-5-2.note: Binds an extended LSP set, which Ze neither originates nor recognizes (owner decision 2026-09-21, standard fragment sets).

RFC3786-6-1.note: Forbidden behaviour: sending IS Hellos (ISH) or IS-IS Hellos with a system-id other than that of the LSP that contains the neighbor. assertNormalHelloIdentity first requires the neighbor in the node's normal LSP, then t.Fatalf when a captured ISH NET system-id or a P2P IIH SystemID differs from lsp.LSPID.SystemID(), and requires both to be seen. TestRFC3786NormalHelloMatchesContainingLSP is the positive; TestRFC3786NormalHelloIdentityReload reloads the NET twice and requires both hellos to follow, so a circuit keeping its old identity goes red. The S' (extended LSP) clause has no producer in Ze (no extended LSP sets), so the normal system-id is the only identity the MUST can require here.
